ON THE FILE OF THE IX C/c. XIII ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, MEMBER,
MACT-7, BENGALURU, (SCCH-15) PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM:
HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri. Vasanthappa learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri.
Sunilkumar.

K learned counsel who represents Sri.H.S.Lingaraj, learned counsel on record for respondent No.2.
2.
Dissatisfied with the amount that is awarded as compensation, the parents of the deceased Murali T.N are before this Court seeking enhancement.
They challenge NC: 2024:KHC:37762 the order that is rendered by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in M.V.C. No.2268/2020 dated 02.03.2022.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Undisputedly, the deceased Murali T. N (hereinafter be referred to as 'deceased' for brevity) died in a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2020.
Projecting a version that the deceased as a Proprietor of M/s Macho Men's Saloon was earning Rs.40,000/- per month, the appellants claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- in total.
However, the tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.17,73,200/- as compensation.
4. Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellants Sri. Vasanthappa contends that the tribunal took the notional income of the deceased as Rs.11,000/- per month which is unjustifiable.
Learned counsel states that the deceased was aged about 22 years by the date of accident and he was earning Rs.40,000/- per month, as a Barber by running a saloon.

Learned counsel also states NC:
2024:KHC:37762 that the accident occurred in the year 2020 and for the relevant period the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as Rs.14,500/- per month and atleast the said figure should have been considered by the tribunal.

Sri. M. Narayanappa vs M. Manjunath on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174187761/
2 5.

entities.text: Sri. M. Narayanappa vs M. Manjunath
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sri. Sunilkumar
. K learned counsel representing respondent No.2 did not raise any objection for taking the notional income of the deceased as Rs.14,500/- per month as sought for.
Also the figure suggested is highly justifiable.

6. As the deceased died at the age of 22 years, 40% of the actual earnings are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Also as the deceased died as Bachelor, 50% of the earnings are required to be deducted towards personal and living expenses which the deceased would have incured for himself had he been alive, as per the decision of the NC: 2024:KHC:37762 Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 SAR (Civ) 592.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 SAR (Civ) 592
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the appropriate multiplier to be applied is '18'.

Thus, applying the aforementioned parameters the amount to be awarded under the head loss of dependency is calculated as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Notional monthly income 14,500-00 Annual income 1,74,000-00 Add 40% towards future 2,43,600-00 prospects

Deduct 50% towards 1,21,800-00 personal and living expenses Apply appropriate multiplier 21,92,400-00 '18'
7.
Thus, the compensation which the appellants are entitled to under the head loss of dependency is Rs.21,92,400/-.
Together with the said amount, the appellants are entitled to Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.44,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

Thus, the total compensation which the appellants are entitled to is as under:-
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Loss of dependency 21,92,400-00 Funeral expenses 16,500-00 Loss of estate 16,500-00
Loss of filial consortium 44,000-00
The tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.17,73,200/- as compensation.
However, the justifiable sum which the appellants are entitled to is Rs.22,69,400/-.

Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The compensation that is awarded by the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru through orders in M.V.C.
No.2268/2020 dated 02.03.2022 is enhanced from Rs.17,73,200/- to Rs.22,69,400/-.

iv. The 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v. On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw their respective shares.
